scope: Northern Rivers local councils and NSW/national programs relevant to community, food systems, environment and resilience. Not an exhaustive list of all business or specialist grants.
verificationNotes: Funders’ official pages and application portals checked on 17 October 2026.
Kyogle’s current website was verified in a browser because its new page was not accessible to web text retrieval; older indexed pages describe a different, closed round.
Tweed pages block direct automated/browser access; official indexed pages and Council announcements are cited. Rolling grants remain subject to available funds.
Exact NSW times are stored as UTC instants. Date-only deadlines stay visible through the published day, with an instruction to confirm the cutoff.
The EPA Streets to Sea portal resolves the 26/27 October discrepancy; only existing Stream 3 grantees are eligible.

notAdded.title: Lismore Rural Landholders Initiative
notAdded.reason: Council says expressions of interest open annually in November. No current open 2026 round or closing date was confirmed.

entries.title: Ballina Shire Council - Community Donations
entries.summary: Small support pathway for community initiatives in Ballina Shire.
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible community organisations in Ballina Shire
entries.notes: Not currently accepting applications. The next published window is 1–31 May 2027 for projects in the 2027/28 financial year. Check Council before preparing an application.

entries.title: Ballina Shire Council - Resource Recovery Community Grants
entries.summary: Supports circular economy and waste minimisation community projects.
entries.funding: Project funding assessed by Council; $50,000 annual program pool
entries.whoCanApply: Individuals, organisations and community groups delivering waste reduction or resource recovery projects within Ballina Shire.
entries.notes: Applications are accepted year-round, with one application per applicant each year. Allow up to six weeks for assessment. The $50,000 figure is the whole annual pool, not an individual grant. Confirm remaining funds with Council.

entries.title: Byron Shire Council - Community Initiatives Grant
entries.summary: Small local grant supporting practical community benefit projects.
entries.whoCanApply: Incorporated community organisations and groups with auspice arrangements in Byron Shire
entries.notes: The 2026 round closed on 5 June 2026. No new application window was confirmed in this review.

entries.title: Clarence Valley Council - Community Initiatives Program
entries.summary: Broad community support program with multiple assistance types.
entries.funding: Cash, rates relief or fee waivers; average award about $1,000
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible incorporated organisations, groups with an ABN and bank account, or auspiced individuals delivering community benefit in Clarence Valley.
entries.notes: Round 2 of 2026/27 is open. Applications close at midnight at the end of 31 October 2026 (AEDT). Applicants may apply in only one round per financial year; read the category conditions. The average award is not a guaranteed amount.
entries.eligibilitySummary: For Clarence Valley community projects; applicants may apply in only one round per financial year.

entries.title: Clarence Valley Council - Sustainable Agriculture Small Grants
entries.summary: Thematic grant aligned to sustainable agriculture and food systems.
entries.funding: Up to $5,000 including GST; matching cash or in-kind contribution required
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible groups or applicants in Clarence Valley context
entries.notes: The 2026–27 round closed at 5 pm on 31 March 2026. Eligible projects must benefit rural-zoned land in Clarence Valley. Check the next round with Council.

entries.title: Community Building Partnership 2026
entries.summary: NSW Government grants for small local infrastructure projects that strengthen community wellbeing.
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible local community organisations and councils including incorporated associations, public companies limited by guarantee, Local Aboriginal Land Councils, Indigenous corporations, NSW local councils, section 355 committees, ACNC-registered trusts, and registered P&C Associations.
entries.notes: The 2026 application round closed at 5 pm on 8 May 2026. Check the provider for future rounds.

entries.title: Community Resilience Grants Program
entries.summary: Supports local Northern Rivers not-for-profit organisations providing critical services and recovery support after the 2022 floods.
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible not-for-profit organisations delivering flood recovery and/or resilience services to people in the 7 Northern Rivers LGAs, with annual gross revenue below $5 million.
entries.notes: The listed program is closed. Check the provider for any future funding announcement.

entries.title: FRRR - Strengthening Rural Communities: Small & Vital
entries.summary: Community-led regional projects with practical local benefit.
entries.funding: Small grants up to $10,000; targeted Larger Leverage grants up to $50,000
entries.whoCanApply: Not-for-profit organisations, or groups with an eligible auspice, benefiting rural, remote or very remote Australian communities. Small grants prioritise communities with fewer than 15,000 residents; check the guidelines for your location.
entries.notes: Round 31 closes at 5 pm AEDT on 3 December 2026. Apply to only one SRC stream per round. The $50,000 tier has narrower priorities: digital inclusion is relevant nationally, while its climate/environment focus is restricted to the Carwarp area in Victoria and does not cover Northern Rivers projects.

entries.title: Kyogle Council - Community Grant Program
entries.summary: Community grant support for projects and events with local benefit.
entries.whoCanApply: Not-for-profit organisations and individuals in the Kyogle LGA
entries.notes: Council’s current website confirms applications opened on 1 October and close on 1 November 2026. No closing time is published; confirm it with Council. Older indexed pages refer to the earlier closed round.
entries.eligibilitySummary: For not-for-profits and individuals delivering community benefit in Kyogle LGA.

entries.title: Lismore Grants Hub
entries.summary: Directory resource to discover current local and regional opportunities.
entries.whoCanApply: A search and alert service for the Lismore community; individual grants have their own eligibility rules.
entries.notes: A Council-supported grant search and alert service, rather than a funding round. Follow through to the relevant provider to check each opportunity.

entries.title: NSW EPA – Business Food Waste Partnership Grants
entries.summary: Supports organisations working with food-wasting businesses to reduce and source-separate food waste ahead of NSW FOGO requirements.
entries.whoCanApply: Peak bodies, sector leaders, councils, educators and other relevant organisations working with food-wasting businesses.
entries.notes: The EPA currently marks this program closed. The latest published Round 3 ran from 26 August to 21 October 2025; do not treat that historical October date as a 2026 deadline.

entries.title: NSW EPA – Food Rescue Grants
entries.summary: Supports organisations expanding food rescue and relief capacity to safely manage increasing amounts of rescued food in NSW.
entries.funding: Previous round: up to $100,000 for individual organisations; up to $300,000 for coordinating organisations
entries.whoCanApply: Food rescue and/or relief organisations and coordinating organisations such as not-for-profits, NSW councils, NSW local government regional waste groups or regional organisations of councils.
entries.notes: Round 2 closed at 4 pm on 21 October 2025. The EPA’s current grants directory still lists the program as closed. No new deadline was verified.

entries.title: NSW Environmental Trust – Environmental Education
entries.summary: Funds projects that build skills and drive behaviour change to improve environmental outcomes.
entries.funding: Tier 1: up to $60,000 per project; Tier 2: $60,001 to $250,000 per project
entries.whoCanApply: Community groups, not-for-profit organisations, state and local government, non-commercial cooperatives, councils, universities, regional organisations of councils, NSW local Aboriginal Land Councils, and registered NSW Aboriginal Corporations.
entries.notes: The 2026–27 round closes at 11:59 pm AEDT on 9 November 2026. Tier 1 supports 2–3 year projects; Tier 2 supports 3–5 year projects. Projects must address a Trust priority, such as biodiversity restoration or environmental management.
entries.eligibilitySummary: For eligible not-for-profits, councils and other approved organisations delivering NSW environmental education.

entries.title: NSW Environmental Trust – Environmental Restoration and Rehabilitation
entries.summary: Supports projects that protect, conserve and restore the NSW environment.
entries.whoCanApply: State and local government and community groups.
entries.notes: The 2026 round closed on 13 May 2026. The provider lists the next opening as April 2027.

entries.title: NSW Environmental Trust – Protecting Our Places
entries.summary: Encourages and empowers Aboriginal communities to protect, conserve and restore landscapes and waterways important to them.
entries.whoCanApply: NSW Aboriginal community organisations or groups.
entries.notes: The 2026 round is closed. The provider lists the next opening as June 2027.

entries.title: Northern Rivers Community Foundation - Community Grants Program
entries.summary: Region-specific grant program for social and environmental projects.
entries.whoCanApply: Not-for-profit groups and eligible community organisations in the seven Northern Rivers LGAs
entries.notes: The 2026–27 round closed on 20 September 2026. Check the provider for future rounds.

entries.title: Northern Rivers Community Foundation - Recovery and Resilience Grants Program
entries.summary: Disaster recovery and preparedness support for impacted communities.
entries.whoCanApply: Northern Rivers not-for-profit community groups impacted by disaster
entries.notes: This is a legacy program page without an advertised open application round. Kept for reference; ask NRCF about current disaster recovery support. Do not assume the historic program is accepting applications.

entries.title: Richmond Valley Council - Community Financial Assistance Program
entries.summary: Small grants for grassroots projects and community events.
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible community groups in the Richmond Valley
entries.notes: The 2026/27 Round 1 closed at 5 pm on 7 October 2026. Council normally runs another round in March; confirm the next dates before applying.

entries.title: Tweed Shire Council - Community Grants Program
entries.summary: Funding for community-led projects that strengthen local connection and care.
entries.whoCanApply: Community groups and not-for-profits in the Tweed region
entries.notes: The 2026 round ran from 1 to 30 June. Council now publishes the successful recipients; no new application round was verified.

entries.title: FRRR — Strengthening Rural Communities: Prepare & Recover
entries.summary: Support for community-led projects that prepare rural and regional places for climate-related disasters or help with medium- to long-term recovery.
entries.whoCanApply: Australian not-for-profits with an ABN or incorporation, or groups using an eligible auspice, with a charitable project benefiting a rural, remote or regional community.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Australian not-for-profits with an ABN or incorporation, or groups using an eligible auspice, with a charitable project benefiting a rural, remote or regional community.
entries.notes: Round 31 closes at 5 pm AEDT on 3 December 2026. Applicants may choose only one SRC stream per round. Funding is announced in March 2027; do not start funded work before the announcement.

entries.title: Ballina Shire Council — Festivals and Events Funding 2027/28
entries.summary: Funding for festivals and events held in Ballina Shire, including larger community gatherings with a clear local benefit.
entries.funding: Approximately $150,000 total program pool; individual awards assessed by Council
entries.whoCanApply: Event organisers with adequate public liability insurance. The event must be held in Ballina Shire and its total cost must exceed $20,000.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Ballina events costing more than $20,000; public liability insurance required. Funding starts July 2027.
entries.notes: Applications close on 6 November 2026; Council does not publish a closing time on the information page. Funding is available from 1 July 2027 for the 2027/28 financial year. Confirm the time and full policy requirements.

entries.title: Clarence Valley Council — Special Event Sponsorship, Round 2
entries.summary: Sponsorship for events that attract visitors to Clarence Valley and encourage them to return.
entries.funding: Award assessed under Council’s sponsorship guidelines
entries.whoCanApply: Organisers of eligible visitor-attracting events in Clarence Valley. First-time applicants should speak to Council’s Event Development Officer.
entries.eligibilitySummary: For visitor-attracting Clarence Valley events between February and July; speak to Council about eligibility.
entries.notes: The 2026/27 Round 2 portal closes at midnight at the end of 31 October 2026 (AEDT). This round supports events between February and July. Read the event criteria before applying.

entries.title: NSW EPA — Streets to Sea: Phase 1 Expression of Interest
entries.summary: An entry stage for catchment-based litter prevention initiatives that reduce waste entering rivers, estuaries and the sea.
entries.funding: Up to $1 million per applicant through the full program; EOI is the first stage
entries.whoCanApply: Only organisations already funded under Stream 3 of the NSW EPA WASM Litter Prevention program, with their Stream 3 initiative underway.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Restricted: existing WASM Stream 3 grantees only. This deadline is for the first-stage EOI.
entries.notes: The application portal confirms midnight at the end of 26 October 2026 (AEDT) for this EOI. Some EPA overview text says 27 October; the live submission portal takes precedence. This is restricted to existing Stream 3 grantees and is not a general small community grant. Later funding applications follow further program stages.

entries.title: Tweed Shire Council — Sustainable Agriculture Small Grants
entries.summary: Practical support for farm projects improving soil, water, biodiversity and sustainable land management in the Tweed.
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible primary producers, market gardeners and small-lot farmers undertaking environmentally beneficial work in Tweed Shire.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Eligible primary producers, market gardeners and small-lot farmers undertaking environmentally beneficial work in Tweed Shire.
entries.notes: The 2026–27 first assessment date was 30 August 2026. Council says later applications remain accepted while funding is available; unfunded applications may move to the next round. Contact the Sustainable Agriculture team on 02 6670 2400 before applying to check remaining funds and eligibility.

entries.title: Tweed Shire Council — River Health Grants
entries.summary: Assistance for riparian restoration, bank erosion, revegetation and keeping livestock out of waterways to improve water quality.
entries.funding: Project funding and support assessed by Council
entries.whoCanApply: Rural landowners in Tweed Shire proposing work that improves water quality or stream health. Priority includes protecting drinking-water catchments.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Rural landowners in Tweed Shire proposing work that improves water quality or stream health. Priority includes protecting drinking-water catchments.
entries.notes: Council invites expressions of interest followed by a site assessment. No fixed deadline or individual grant cap is published. Confirm current funding, site suitability and any required approvals with Council before starting work.
